Every rule id in card-data.md's Lint table, ported from tomada-routine's

entry.content:
feat: add the study session end to end — session, review and end APIs, the study screen and the summary (#26)

* feat: add the session, review and end APIs behind a composition root

The first Route Handlers this repository ships, and the first place the
environment, the database and a handler are joined.

Each handler is a `create<Name>Handler(dependencies)` factory under
`src/server/handlers/`, taking its store, its deck and its clock as
arguments, so a test drives it with a plain `new Request(...)` against
`:memory:`. `src/server/composition.ts` is the one file that chooses the
concrete three: it reads `VOCAB_DB_PATH` through `src/server/env.ts`,
opens the database once per process — lazily, so a route module imported
during `next build` creates no file — and each route under
`src/app/api/sessions/` is a single re-export line over what it built.

The session id of the two `[id]` routes is read off the request's own
URL rather than taken as a second argument, which is what keeps every
handler `Request`-only and every route file logic-free.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DFx7GEDTyxoPhqjr85cskK

* feat: add the study screen and the session summary

`/[locale]/study` opens a session on mount, shows a card's definition and
cloze, reveals the headword and both examples on Space or Enter, rates it
with 1-4 or the four buttons, and keeps a remaining count. A card the
review answer requeues goes back to the end of the local queue — the
20-minute learn-ahead rule stated once in `src/core/session.ts` and read
from both sides. Esc, or an empty queue, ends the session and moves to
`/[locale]/sessions/[id]`, which reports the ratings recorded and the
change in remembered-now. Its daily curve is issue #10's.

Only `study-session.tsx` carries `"use client"`; the page above it stays
a Server Component, and the summary page opts its own route out of the
locale layout's `force-static` because it is a database read.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DFx7GEDTyxoPhqjr85cskK

* test: cover the session-id path read and an unknown stored phase

Three branches of `session-context.ts` the handler suite reached only one
side of: a path segment that is not a number, the same id read through a
trailing slash, and a `card_state` row whose phase is outside the four
FSRS knows — which must degrade to New rather than end the session it
turns up in.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DFx7GEDTyxoPhqjr85cskK

* fix: correct the study session's client/server field mismatch and dedupe id parsing

Code review found the client's OpenSession type naming the session id field
`id` while the server actually answers `sessionId` — an unnoticed mismatch
because the test's fetch stub fabricated the wrong client shape instead of
the real handler response, so every existing test passed while the whole
study flow was broken end to end in production. Renamed the field
consistently across the client, the study page and the test stub.

Also extracts session-context.ts's session-id validation into a shared
parseSessionId, so the summary page and the handlers cannot silently
disagree on what counts as a valid id.

Two lower-severity findings from the same review are deferred: repeated
full-table Store reads on the review hot path (#27), and the corrupted-state
handling in toPhase, which needs a design decision (#28).

entry.title: feat: add scope filtering, the IELTS→CEFR target table and the progre…
entry.content:
feat: add scope filtering, the IELTS→CEFR target table and the progress math (#24)

* feat: add scope filtering and the IELTS to CEFR target table

`src/core/scope.ts` holds the Scope type and its strict zod schema, the
IELTS band to CEFR table written out band by band, `targetLevels` (the
band's level plus the one below it) and `inScope`, the four conditions
that decide whether a card is one a scope selects.

The table is an `as const satisfies Record<IeltsScore, Level>` rather
than a set of ranges, so a band added to IELTS_SCORES fails to compile
until it is mapped.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DFx7GEDTyxoPhqjr85cskK

* feat: add the progress math behind every number a scope shows

`src/core/progress.ts` adds `rememberedNow` (the sum of the FSRS recall
probability over the reviewed, non-retired cards in scope),
`unlearnedCount`, `targetRatio`, and `dailyCurve` — one point per study
day from the first in-scope review's day to today, each at that day's
04:00 rollover, with today's point taken at now so the last point always
equals remembered now.

Every figure is recomputed from the review history, never snapshotted,
which is what lets a scope the owner has never selected before show the
same history as one they have always used. The curve walks the ratings
once in time order alongside the days, so the 3,000 cards over 365 days
the design budgets for stay one closed-form evaluation per card per day.

entry.title: feat: add ts-fsrs and the scheduler wrapper with the 04:00 rollover (…
entry.content:
feat: add ts-fsrs and the scheduler wrapper with the 04:00 rollover (#22)

`src/core/scheduler.ts` is the only module that imports `ts-fsrs`, and it
publishes plain numbers: a `Rating` union, a `SchedulerState` mirroring the
`card_state` table with every instant an epoch-millisecond number, and
`rate`/`retrievability`/`dayBounds` over them. Swapping the library is
therefore a bounded edit, and `tests/boundaries.test.ts` holds that to one
importer the same way it holds `node:sqlite` to `src/server/db/`.

The FSRS parameters are the ones settled in `building-the-vocab-app`'s
storage-and-scheduling reference — 90% requested retention, fuzz on, short-term
scheduling on — with the weights and the (re)learning steps left at ts-fsrs's
defaults. Fuzz is seeded from the card and the review time, so `rate` answers
the same for the same arguments.

`dayBounds` reads both ends of a study day off the zone's wall clock rather
than deriving one from the other, so a day across a DST change is 23 or 25
hours long rather than silently shifting the rollover.

`ts-fsrs` is declared as a SemVer range, per `managing-dependencies`; 5.4.2 is
MIT, has no runtime dependencies of its own, and was published on 2026-09-01,
past the `minimumReleaseAge` cooldown.

Closes #5

entry.title: docs: add the reviewing-cards skill — blind answer and perspective re…
entry.content:
docs: add the reviewing-cards skill — blind answer and perspective review (#20)

* docs: add the reviewing-cards skill and its two lenses

The mechanical Lint sees only shape, so whether a front has exactly one
answer is reviewed by an independent run instead. The doctrine is adapted
from tomada-routine's anki-router review-doctrine.md and the
anki-vocabulary section of short-form-review.md: pass only the criteria
text and the cards, ask for violations, return only failing cards, DROP
beats FIX, and DROP is advice the calling session decides on.

The blind-answer run is handed the definition and the cloze alone — not
even the card id, which is derived from the headword — and returns the
words that fit; the caller compares that list against the real headword.
The perspective run sees the whole card and the existing card list, and
holds five criteria: answer leak by paraphrase, example quality,
disguised echo, overlapping examples, duplicate synonym.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DFx7GEDTyxoPhqjr85cskK

* test: assert the reviewing-cards prompts and output shape

A skill that is pasted into another run is a contract: the blind-answer
template must be fed the definition and the cloze and nothing else, each
perspective criterion must reach the run with its text rather than its
name, and the worked outputs in SKILL.md must match the shape the calling
session parses. agents:check only proves the mirror matches and the
frontmatter suite only reads frontmatter, so none of that had a gate.

The suite joins the automation project: it asserts against files on disk
rather than against imported code.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DFx7GEDTyxoPhqjr85cskK

* fix: correct two self-contradictions in the blind-answer lens doc

Code review found the doc claiming the run "does not decide the card's fate"
when its own prompt spec has it emit a self-judged FIX/DROP for every
ambiguous or empty word list, and claiming the table's last two rows
(Empty, Only true synonyms) are the ones needing the caller's headword
knowledge, when both are already self-flagged by the run — the row that
actually needs the caller is the third one, where a single wrong word
produces no finding at all and silently looks like a pass.

entry.title: feat: add the SQLite store — node:sqlite connection, migrations and q…
entry.content:
feat: add the SQLite store — node:sqlite connection, migrations and queries (#18)

* feat: add the SQLite store under src/server/db/

Opens a node:sqlite DatabaseSync in WAL mode with the migrations applied on
open, creates card_state, review_log, session and setting exactly as
storage-and-scheduling.md's "The database" states them, and binds the query
surface every later storage-touching issue calls.

The migration list is ordered SQL tracked by PRAGMA user_version and applied
inside one transaction, so a file is never left half-migrated. The tables are
STRICT, which is what makes a row readable back as the record it was written
from: an INTEGER epoch-millisecond column cannot quietly hold a fraction.
One rating is one transaction — the card_state upsert and the review_log
insert land together or not at all.

tests/boundaries.test.ts now holds node:sqlite to src/server/db/ from the
module graph, so no page or handler can open a second connection without the
pragmas openDatabase applies.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DFx7GEDTyxoPhqjr85cskK

* feat: add the optional VOCAB_DB_PATH setting

Declares where the SQLite store lives, defaulting to the gitignored
.data/english-vocab.sqlite. Unlike the other name env.ts reads, an absent or
blank value resolves to that default rather than to undefined: there is always
a database, and a caller supplying the fallback itself would be the second
place the path is written down.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DFx7GEDTyxoPhqjr85cskK

* test: cover the guarded rollback in withTransaction

A ROLLBACK with no transaction open raises, so the guard is what keeps the
caller's own failure from being replaced by one about transaction state.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DFx7GEDTyxoPhqjr85cskK

* fix: harden the SQLite store against nesting, corruption and unserializable values

Code review (high effort) on the storage layer turned up seven real gaps:
withTransaction had no reentrancy guard and its rollback checks could mask the
original failure with a secondary one; openDatabase never set a busy timeout,
contradicting its own WAL rationale; toJson only guarded JSON.stringify
returning undefined, not it raising for a circular reference or a BigInt;
readUserVersion could return a negative version that MIGRATIONS.slice would
silently misread, and a failure there escaped the DatabaseError contract.

Also splits the single ERR_DB_VALUE_INVALID code into three
(ERR_DB_VALUE_UNSERIALIZABLE, ERR_DB_VALUE_CORRUPT,
ERR_DB_VALUE_SCHEMA_MISMATCH) so a caller can tell an unserializable input
from a corrupted file from a stale schema.

entry.content:
feat: add the card schema, id derivation, topic/purpose lists and the card loader (#17)

* feat: add the card schema, id derivation and the data lists

A strict zod schema for one vocabulary card, matching the field table in
`building-the-vocab-app`'s card-data reference, plus the `cardId` derivation
that turns a card's `(headword, pos)` key into its id and its file name.

The committed lists come with it: the 15 topic ids and the single `ielts`
purpose, beside the empty `data/cards/` tree the generator will fill. Topic
and purpose membership, and every rule about a card's text, belong to the
Lint rather than to the schema.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DFx7GEDTyxoPhqjr85cskK

* feat: add the card loader, the only reader of data/

`loadCards` returns every card a directory holds beside one error per file
that is not one — unreadable, not JSON, off-schema, or named something other
than the id it declares — and never throws, so one bad file cannot hide the
cards beside it or end the page that asked for them.

`loadLists` throws instead, because a missing or malformed topic or purpose
list leaves no vocabulary to build a scope out of at all: a repository
mistake with no caller-side recovery, read the way `src/server/env.ts` reads
the environment.

Its suite joins `automationTests` because it reads the disk, including the
committed `data/` tree, which is what makes a malformed list file fail CI
rather than the first page that asks for one.
